definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\text{ in a bow-ADMG SCM with }\Pr(A=a)=e,\ \mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P,\text{ and member properties }\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:positivity},\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\}\). At the boundary, define \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\text{ with }R\ll P\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
definitions.construction: \(\{f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R: f\text{ is finite, continuous, convex, }f(1)=0,\text{ and there exists }b\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }g_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\text{ obeys }g_b(t)=0\text{ for }0\le t\le c\text{ and }g_b(t)>0\text{ for }t>c\}\).

definitions.name: \(L_e,U_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\), \(L_e(p)=e p\) for \(0\le p<1\), \(L_e(1)=1\), \(U_e(0)=0\), and \(U_e(p)=e p+1-e\) for \(0<p\le1\). In particular, \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(n_a=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), \(\delta_e=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)}\), and \(\delta_F=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n_a)}\) when \(n_a>0\). Form \(I_e=[\widehat e_n-\delta_e,\widehat e_n+\delta_e]\cap[0,1]\) and \(I_F(y)=[\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-\delta_F,\widehat F_{P,n}(y)+\delta_F]\cap[0,1]\). For every \(y\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\) is the coordinatewise rectangular hull of \(\{(L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p)):\eta\in I_e,\ p\in I_F(y)\}\); when \(n_a=0\), set it to \([0,1]^2\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\)
definitions.construction: Handle: linearize the joint pre-endpoint empirical process \((\widehat e_n,\widehat F_{P,n})\), derive the Hadamard directional derivative of the piecewise map \((e,F_P)\mapsto(L_e\circ F_P,U_e\circ F_P)\), and estimate that derivative inside a Fang--Santos multiplier or numerical-delta bootstrap before taking the supremum over thresholds and arms.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\) is the set of laws \(Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\) realized in a nonparametric latent-variable bow-ADMG SCM with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P\), and member properties \(\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), without imposing \(\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\). At the boundary define \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y):Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(L^{\to}_e,U^{\to}_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\) and \(0\le p\le1\), define \(L^{\to}_e(p)=ep\) and \(U^{\to}_e(p)=ep+1-e\).

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), the bow-ADMG compatible interventional laws are exactly the propensity mixtures: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\). Equivalently, \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\) if and only if \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\), or if and only if \(Q\sim P\) and \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) \(Q\)-almost surely. Every admissible \(R\) is realized by a latent construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\).
statements.justification: This structural input identifies the exact compatible-SCM law set needed by the flagship generator frontier.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that compatible interventional laws lie in the calibrated ambiguity class, while Huber contamination results do not prove realization by the specified bow SCM.
statements.consumer: It supplies the legal feasible set for every downstream distributional or expectation bound in \(\texttt{itbound}\).
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\), every unrestricted compatible law has a representation \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary \(R\), and every such representation is realized.  Consistency identifies \(P=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\).  The maintained mutual-absolute-continuity assumption is therefore exactly the additional condition \(Q\ll P\), since \(P\ll Q\) already follows from \(Q\ge eP\).  For the displayed representation,
\[
 Q\ll P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R\ll P:
\]
the forward implication follows from \((1-e)R\le Q\) and \(1-e>0\), and the reverse implication follows by summing two measures absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\).  Hence
\[
 \mathfrak M_e(P)=\{eP+(1-e)R:R\ll P\}=\mathfrak L_e(P).
\]
The one-sided cap characterization in the cited theorem, intersected with \(Q\ll P\), gives equivalently \(Q\sim P\) and \(dP/dQ\le1/e\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  The cited latent construction has \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\); the preceding equivalence shows that it satisfies the mutual support assumption exactly for \(R\ll P\).  This proves the theorem as stated.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.justification: This is the flagship result: the affine-invariant iff identifies precisely which divergence ambiguity classes are causally complete rather than merely valid outer sets.
statements.gap: Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018) preserve least-favorable tests under a constructed density band and ask when uncertainty sets themselves coincide; Jung and Kang (2026) do not characterize the generators giving set equality.
statements.consumer: Divergence designers obtain a complete rule for selecting a propensity-calibrated generator whose feasible laws are exactly the bow-SCM laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\) and put \(c=1/e\).  We first record two consequences of the definitions.  If \(P\ll Q\) and \(r=dP/dQ\), then
\[
 \int r\,dQ=1.
\]
Consequently, replacing \(f\) by \(f_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) leaves both relevant quantities unchanged:
\[
 D_{f_b}(P\|Q)=D_f(P\|Q),\qquad
 B_{f_b}(e)=B_f(e)-b\{e(c-1)-(1-e)\}=B_f(e).
\]
Also, convexity on \([0,c]\) gives the chord inequality
\[
 f(t)\le \left(1-\frac{t}{c}\right)f(0)+\frac{t}{c}f(c),\qquad 0\le t\le c. \tag{1}
\]
If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\), then \(Q\ge eP\), so \(P\ll Q\) and \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely; moreover \(Q\ll P\).  Integrating (1) therefore yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le f(0)+\frac{f(c)-f(0)}{c}\int r\,dQ
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\) for every admissible \(f\).

Suppose first that \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak H_c\), there is \(b\in\mathbb R\) such that \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) is zero on \([0,c]\) and strictly positive on \((c,\infty)\).  Affine invariance gives \(B_g(e)=B_f(e)=0\).  For \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), mutual absolute continuity supplies \(r=dP/dQ>0\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and
\[
 0\le \int g(r)\,dQ=D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)=0.
\]
Hence \(g(r)=0\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and therefore \(r\le c\).  The finite measure \(Q-eP\) has density \(1-er\ge0\) with respect to \(Q\), has total mass \(1-e\), and is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\) because \(Q\ll P\).  Thus
\[
 R=\frac{Q-eP}{1-e}
\]
is a probability law satisfying \(R\ll P\), and \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  This proves \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\subseteq\mathfrak L_e(P)\); the reverse inclusion is (2).  Exactness follows for every \(P\).

Conversely, assume exactness for every full-support binary \(P\).  Fix \(p\in(0,1)\), set \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), and let \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(ep)\).  The representation
\[
 Q_0=eP+(1-e)\operatorname{Bernoulli}(0)
\]
places \(Q_0\) in \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\), because every binary law is absolutely continuous with respect to the full-support law \(P\).  If \(0<q<ep\), then for \(Q_q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\),
\[
 \frac{P(\{1\})}{Q_q(\{1\})}=\frac pq>c,
\]
so \(Q_q\notin\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  Exactness and full support imply
\[
 D_f(P\|Q_q)>B_f(e)\quad(0<q<ep),
 \qquad D_f(P\|Q_0)\le B_f(e).
\]
The binary divergence is continuous in \(q\in(0,1)\), since \(f\) is finite and continuous.  Letting \(q\uparrow ep\) proves
\[
 D_f(P\|Q_0)=B_f(e). \tag{3}
\]
At \(Q_0\), the two likelihood ratios are \(c\) and
\[
 t_p=\frac{1-p}{1-ep},
\]
so (3) reads
\[
 ep f(c)+(1-ep)f(t_p)=B_f(e). \tag{4}
\]
Letting \(p\downarrow0\) in (4), using \(t_p\to1\), continuity, and \(f(1)=0\), gives \(B_f(e)=0\).

Set \(b=-f(0)\) and \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\).  The identity \(B_f(e)=0\), equivalently \(f(c)+(c-1)f(0)=0\), gives
\[
 g(0)=g(c)=g(1)=0. \tag{5}
\]
By affine invariance, (4) and (5) imply \(g(t_p)=0\).  As \(p\) ranges over \((0,1)\), \(t_p\) ranges over \((0,1)\); hence \(g=0\) on \([0,1]\).  Now fix \(y\in(1,c)\) and any \(x\in(0,1)\), and set
\[
 \lambda=\frac{1-x}{y-x}\in(0,1).
\]
There are full-support binary laws whose likelihood ratio \(dP/dQ\) equals \(y\) on the success cell of \(Q\)-mass \(\lambda\) and equals \(x\) on the other cell, because
\[
 \lambda y+(1-\lambda)x=1.
\]
Their likelihood ratio is at most \(c\), so the preceding measure construction places \(Q\) in \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  Exactness and \(B_g(e)=0\) give
\[
 0\ge D_g(P\|Q)=\lambda g(y)+(1-\lambda)g(x)=\lambda g(y).
\]
On the other hand, convexity at \(1=\lambda y+(1-\lambda)x\) gives \(0=g(1)\le D_g(P\|Q)\).  Therefore \(g(y)=0\).  Together with (5), this proves \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\).

For \(t>c\), write \(c\) as a strict convex combination of \(1\) and \(t\).  Convexity and \(g(1)=g(c)=0\) imply \(g(t)\ge0\).  If \(g(t)=0\) for some \(t>c\), repeat the preceding two-ratio construction with \(y=t\).  It gives full-support binary laws with \(D_g(P\|Q)=0=B_g(e)\), hence \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), but with likelihood ratio \(t>c\), hence \(Q\notin\mathfrak L_e(P)\), a contradiction.  Thus \(g(t)>0\) for every \(t>c\), which is exactly \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).

We have proved the equivalence between universal exactness, binary exactness, and membership in \(\mathfrak H_c\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) identifies \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\) with the bow-SCM compatible class \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\), so the equality characterized above is causal rather than merely an equality of abstract probability-law classes.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of binary pairs \((p,q)\), interpreted as \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\) throughout \(\mathcal O_f\). More precisely, either no affine representative of \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), in which case \(\mathcal O_f\) can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\), or an affine representative vanishes on \([0,c]\) and on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), in which case an open illegal set is contained in the zero-divergence face. This dichotomy includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.justification: This stable converse certifies that every failure of the flagship frontier persists under perturbation and is not a hand-tuned counterexample.
statements.gap: Sason and Verdu (2016) analyze hinge divergences and bounded likelihood ratios, while Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014) reduce divergence extrema to small alphabets; neither proves this fully quantified open-set dichotomy for every finite convex generator.
statements.consumer: The result gives a robust legality diagnostic for KL, Hellinger, chi-square, total-variation, Jensen--Shannon, and every other failing generator.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), put \(c=1/e\), and define the chord of \(f\) between \(0\) and \(c\) by
\[
 \ell(t)=\left(1-\frac tc\right)f(0)+\frac tc f(c).
\]
Convexity gives \(f(t)\le\ell(t)\) on \([0,c]\), and
\[
 \ell(1)=(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{6}
\]
Subtracting an affine function does not change whether a function is affine on an interval.  Thus the first case in the statement is precisely the case in which \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\).

Assume first that \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\).  Then
\[
 f(x)<\ell(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in(0,c). \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, \(h=\ell-f\) is concave and nonnegative on \([0,c]\), with \(h(0)=h(c)=0\).  If \(h(x_0)=0\) at one interior point, concavity applied first with endpoints \(x<x_0<c\) and then with endpoints \(0<x_0<x\) forces \(h(x)=0\) on both sides of \(x_0\), contradicting non-affinity.

Choose \(x\in(0,1)\), let
\[
 \lambda=\frac{1-x}{c-x},\qquad q_0=\lambda,\qquad p_0=c\lambda,
\]
and put \(P_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\), \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_0)\).  Since \(c>1\) and \(0<x<1\), both laws have full support.  Their likelihood ratios are \(c\) and \(x\), and \(q_0=ep_0\), so \(Q_0\in\mathfrak L_e(P_0)\).  Because affine functions commute with expectation and the two ratios have \(Q_0\)-mean one, (6)--(7) give
\[
 D_f(P_0\|Q_0)
 =\lambda f(c)+(1-\lambda)f(x)
 <\lambda\ell(c)+(1-\lambda)\ell(x)
 =\ell(1)=B_f(e). \tag{8}
\]
The binary divergence is continuous on \((0,1)^2\).  Hence one may choose \(q_1<q_0=ep_0\), sufficiently close to \(q_0\), such that
\[
 D_f\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\middle\|\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_1)\right)<B_f(e).
\]
Both strict inequalities \(D_f<B_f(e)\) and \(q<ep\) persist on some nonempty Euclidean-open neighborhood \(\mathcal O_f\) of \((p_0,q_1)\) contained in \((0,1)^2\).  Throughout this neighborhood, \(P\sim Q\), the strict divergence inequality places \(Q\) in \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), while \(p/q>c\) excludes \(Q\) from \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  This proves the first alternative.

Assume next that \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\).  Since \(f(1)=0\), there is \(b\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
 g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)=0,\qquad 0\le t\le c. \tag{9}
\]
Convexity and (9) imply \(g(t)\ge0\) for \(t>c\).  Because \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), strict positivity fails: there is \(d>c\) with \(g(d)=0\).  Convexity between \(c\) and \(d\), together with nonnegativity, shows that in fact
\[
 g(t)=0,\qquad 0\le t\le d. \tag{10}
\]
Choose \(x\in(0,1)\) and \(y\in(c,d)\), let \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\), and form full-support binary laws for which \(dP/dQ\) equals \(y\) on a cell of \(Q\)-mass \(\lambda\) and \(x\) on its complement.  In Bernoulli coordinates this means \(q=\lambda\) and \(p=\lambda y\).  Then \(p/q=y>c\), so the pair is SCM-illegal, whereas affine invariance and (10) give
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)=D_g(P\|Q)=0=B_g(e)=B_f(e).
\]
The inequalities \(p/q>c\), \((1-p)/(1-q)\in(0,d)\), and \(p/q<d\) persist on a sufficiently small open neighborhood.  On that neighborhood both likelihood ratios lie in \((0,d)\), so (10) keeps the divergence identically zero, while the cap remains violated.  This is the asserted nonempty open illegal set in the zero-divergence face.  The argument uses only finiteness, continuity, and convexity, and therefore includes kinked and piecewise-linear generators.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\). For every threshold \(y\), write \(p=F_P(y)\). The exact bow-SCM identified interval is \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\). Each endpoint is attained by a bow-ADMG SCM satisfying all maintained support conditions, including when \(P\) has an atom at \(y\), \(p=0\), or \(p=1\). For \(0<p<1\), the witnesses choose residual laws supported on \(({-}\infty,y]\) or its complement; the boundary formulas force the unique value \(0\) or \(1\).
statements.justification: This consequence converts the structural mixture input into closed-form distributional endpoints and handles atoms correctly.
statements.gap: Huber contamination gives the scalar mixture geometry and Duarte et al. (2024) certify discrete SCM bounds computationally, but neither supplies these continuous-outcome bow-SCM endpoints with explicit attainment under mutual absolute continuity.
statements.consumer: Researchers reporting counterfactual CDFs or quantiles can replace relaxed divergence endpoints by exact, directly evaluable causal envelopes.
statements.proof_tex:
The support-regime theorem \(\mathrm{thm:support\text{-}regime\text{-}cdf\text{-}endpoints\text{-}sharp}\) proves, in particular, that under mutual absolute continuity
\[
 \{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y))].
\]
It constructs the two conditional residual laws when \(0<F_P(y)<1\), proves that \(R\ll P\) forces the unique value zero or one at the two support boundaries, and realizes each residual law with the latent bow construction.  Those arguments are eventwise and allow atoms at \(y\).  This is exactly the present statement.

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\). For each \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), the exact mutual-AC support-function endpoints are \(\underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h\) and \(\overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h\). On a finite alphabet restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), adding the cap constraints \(q_j\ge ep_j\) to a divergence program yields the exact mutual-AC class, weakly tightens every linear bounded-query optimization, and strictly tightens it whenever a unique relaxed optimizer violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), a bounded binary query has a strict legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational laws.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the cap into an exact feasible-set correction under either explicitly stated optimization ambient space.
statements.gap: The frozen evidence does not establish which support convention the itbound code uses, so the theorem gives both checkable branches instead of guessing.
statements.consumer: A source audit selects the correct branch before the itbound and IHDP re-analysis.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), put \(c=1/e\), and let \(f\) be any finite continuous convex generator with \(f(1)=0\).  If \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\), then \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\).  Thus \(Q\sim P\), and for \(r=dP/dQ\) one has \(0<r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  The convex chord inequality on \([0,c]\) yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le\int\left\{\left(1-\frac rc\right)f(0)+\frac rc f(c)\right\}dQ
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{11}
\]
Hence \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\).  By the definition of the lawful correction,
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\cap\mathfrak L_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L_e(P).
\]
The frozen bow-mixture completeness theorem then gives \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\).

Let \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), and write
\[
 m=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h,\qquad M=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h.
\]
For \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\),
\[
 E_Q[h]=eE_P[h]+(1-e)E_R[h],\qquad m\le E_R[h]\le M. \tag{12}
\]
Thus the claimed expressions bound the infimum and supremum.  Conversely, for every \(\eta>0\), the defining properties of essential infimum and supremum give sets of positive \(P\)-probability
\[
 C^-_\eta=\{h<m+\eta\},\qquad C^+_\eta=\{h>M-\eta\}.
\]
Taking \(R^-_\eta=P(\,\cdot\mid C^-_\eta)\) and \(R^+_\eta=P(\,\cdot\mid C^+_\eta)\), both of which are absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), and then letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) in (12), proves
\[
 \underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)m,\qquad
 \overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)M. \tag{13}
\]

Now suppose the alphabet is finite and restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), so every retained cell has \(p_j>0\).  A probability vector \(q=(q_j)_j\) belongs to \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\) if and only if
\[
 q_j\ge ep_j\quad\text{for every }j. \tag{14}
\]
The forward implication follows from \(q_j=ep_j+(1-e)r_j\).  Conversely, (14) makes
\[
 r_j=\frac{q_j-ep_j}{1-e}
\]
nonnegative with \(\sum_jr_j=1\), and the support restriction gives \(R\ll P\).  By (11), the divergence constraint is redundant on (14).  Therefore adjoining (14) to the divergence program gives exactly the mutual-absolute-continuity compatible class.  Its feasible set is a closed subset of the finite simplex and hence compact.  Restricting a feasible set can only weakly lower a linear maximum and weakly raise a linear minimum.  If a relaxed optimizer is unique and violates (14), equality of the corresponding optimal values would make an optimizer over the compact capped set a second relaxed optimizer, a contradiction.  The tightening is then strict.  The same coordinate argument is consistent with the unrestricted-alphabet formulation in \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}query\text{-}legality\text{-}correction}\).

Finally suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\).  The construction in \(\mathrm{thm:open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\) yields an open binary set with \(q<ep\) and \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\).  It contains a rectangle \(I\times J\) about one of its points.  For every \(p\) in a sufficiently small nonempty open interval \(I\), some \(q\in J\) remains divergence-feasible and satisfies \(q<ep\).  For the bounded success indicator \(h(z)=\mathbf 1\{z=1\}\), the lawful lower endpoint is \(ep\) by (13), whereas the relaxed lower value is at most \(q<ep\).  This is the claimed strict legality gap on an open region of observational laws.

statements.statement: Under independent observational sampling, the band \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\Pr\{(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\text{ for every }y\in\mathbb R\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), including \(n_a=0\), arbitrary atoms, and contact with \(F_P(y)\in\{0,1\}\). The guarantee follows by combining a propensity Hoeffding interval with a conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz band and propagating their joint rectangle through the full piecewise endpoint map.
statements.justification: This inference layer propagates the lawful endpoint consequence with an honest finite-sample simultaneous guarantee at nonsmooth boundary cases.
statements.gap: Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) develop uniform bands over a sensitivity index, and Jung and Kang (2026) give scalar orthogonal inference; neither covers the threshold-indexed lawful endpoint pair with boundary contacts.
statements.consumer: The IHDP audit can report simultaneous uncertainty for the complete corrected CDF envelope rather than pointwise error bars.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), so that the independent-sampling assumption gives independent variables with \(0\le Z_i\le1\) and \(E[Z_i]=e\).  Put
\[
 E_e=\{e\in I_e\}=\{|\widehat e_n-e|\le\delta_e\}.
\]
The equality of the two events is understood after clipping to \([0,1]\): because \(e\in[0,1]\), membership in the un-clipped interval implies membership in \(I_e\).  Since \(n\ge1\) for the sampling construction and \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\delta_e>0\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}bounded\text{-}mean}\) with \(m=n\) and \(t=\delta_e\) yields
\[
 \Pr(E_e^c)
 \le 2\exp(-2n\delta_e^2)
 =2\exp\{-\log(4/\alpha)\}
 =\alpha/2. \tag{1}
\]

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\sigma(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\).  Conditional on \(\mathcal A_n\), on the event \(n_a=m>0\), the variables \(Y_i\) with \(A_i=a\) are independent and each has conditional law \(P=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)\).  This follows directly from the factorization of the joint law of the independent pairs \((A_i,Y_i)\) under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\).  Thus \(\mathrm{lem:dkw\text{-}massart\text{-}cdf\text{-}band}\), conditionally with sample size \(m\) and \(t=\delta_F\), gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(
   \left.\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}
   |\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-F_P(y)|>\delta_F
   \ \right|\mathcal A_n
 \right)
 \le 2\exp(-2m\delta_F^2)
 =\alpha/2. \tag{2}
\]
Define \(E_F\) to be the complementary event in (2) when \(n_a>0\), and define \(E_F\) to hold when \(n_a=0\).  Taking conditional expectations in (2) gives \(\Pr(E_F^c)\le\alpha/2\).  Consequently, the union bound and (1) imply
\[
 \Pr(E_e\cap E_F)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{3}
\]

Suppose first that \(n_a>0\).  On \(E_e\cap E_F\), simultaneously for every \(y\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 (e,F_P(y))\in I_e\times I_F(y). \tag{4}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}band}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\) is the coordinatewise rectangular hull of the image of this rectangle under
\[
 (\eta,p)\longmapsto (L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p)).
\]
Substituting the particular point in (4) therefore gives, for every \(y\),
\[
 (L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))
 \in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y). \tag{5}
\]
This argument is set inclusion and uses neither continuity nor differentiability of the piecewise maps in \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\); hence it also covers atoms and the contacts \(F_P(y)=0\) and \(F_P(y)=1\).  If \(n_a=0\), then \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}band}\) sets the band equal to \([0,1]^2\), and (5) holds because \(L_e(p),U_e(p)\in[0,1]\).  Combining (3)--(5) proves the asserted probability bound.  Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:cdf\text{-}endpoints\text{-}sharp}\) identifies the two coordinates in (5) as the exact mutual-absolute-continuity bow-SCM endpoint functionals, rather than merely as observed-law transformations.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Consider any sequence of rectangular simultaneous bands that has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over a local class. Suppose the class contains a boundary observed-data law with \(F_P(y_0)=1\) and a sequence of alternatives with the same arm propensity \(e\) and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n>0\), \(n\delta_n\to0\), and the total-variation distance between the corresponding \(n\)-sample observed-data laws is \(o(1)\). Under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), the lower-endpoint projection of the band at \(y_0\) has diameter at least \(1-e\). The analogous assertion holds for the upper-endpoint projection when the class contains a boundary law with \(F_P(y_0)=0\) and alternatives with the same propensity and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\), under the same \(n\)-sample total-variation condition. Such alternatives exist within the bow-SCM class whenever \(n\delta_n\to0\). Consequently, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) cannot yield a nonconservative shrinking band uniformly over such a total-variation-local tie-inclusive class; derivative-aware inference is restricted to strata separated from these contacts, with \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) retained as the honest fallback. The extension of \(L_e,U_e\) to \(e=0\) is algebraic and used only by the clipped finite-sample construction; this impossibility result assumes \(0<e<1\).
statements.justification: This negative resolution isolates the discontinuity that prevents uniformly shrinking endpoint bands at drifting support contacts.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) provide derivative-aware bootstrap validity, but that device cannot overcome statistical indistinguishability across the discontinuous lawful endpoint faces proved here.
statements.consumer: The result delineates the separated regular strata where shorter directional bands may be used and retains the honest finite-sample band elsewhere.
statements.proof_tex:
Write an arbitrary rectangular band at \(y\) as
\[
 \mathcal C_n(y)=I_n^L(y)\times I_n^U(y),
\]
where the two factors are random intervals.  The assumed uniform asymptotic coverage means, in particular, that along the boundary law and along every displayed alternative sequence the relevant simultaneous-coverage probability is at least \(1-\alpha-r_n\) for some \(r_n=o(1)\).  Marginal coverage at \(y_0\) follows because the simultaneous-coverage event is a subset of the corresponding marginal event.

First suppose \(F_{P,0}(y_0)=1\), and let \(\mathbb P_{0,n}\) and \(\mathbb P_{1,n}\) denote the boundary and alternative \(n\)-sample observed-data laws.  By \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\), the boundary and alternative lower endpoints are respectively
\[
 \ell_0=L_e(1)=1,
 \qquad
 \ell_n=L_e(1-\delta_n)=e(1-\delta_n), \tag{6}
\]
where the second equality uses \(0<1-\delta_n<1\), which holds for all sufficiently large \(n\) because \(n\delta_n\to0\) and \(\delta_n>0\).  Let
\[
 C_{0,n}=\{\ell_0\in I_n^L(y_0)\},
 \qquad
 C_{1,n}=\{\ell_n\in I_n^L(y_0)\}.
\]
Uniform coverage gives
\[
 \mathbb P_{0,n}(C_{0,n})\ge1-\alpha-o(1),
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{1,n}(C_{1,n})\ge1-\alpha-o(1). \tag{7}
\]
For any event \(C\), the definition of total-variation distance gives
\[
 |\mathbb P_{0,n}(C)-\mathbb P_{1,n}(C)|
 \le \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_{0,n},\mathbb P_{1,n}).
\]
The assumed \(o(1)\) total-variation distance and (7) therefore imply \(\mathbb P_{0,n}(C_{1,n})\ge1-\alpha-o(1)\).  Bonferroni's inequality now gives
\[
 \mathbb P_{0,n}(C_{0,n}\cap C_{1,n})
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1). \tag{8}
\]
On this intersection the interval \(I_n^L(y_0)\) contains both values in (6), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{diam} I_n^L(y_0)
 \ge |\ell_0-\ell_n|
 =1-e+e\delta_n
 \ge1-e. \tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) prove the lower-endpoint assertion.

If instead \(F_{P,0}(y_0)=0\) and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\), then \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 u_0=U_e(0)=0,
 \qquad
 u_n=U_e(\delta_n)=1-e+e\delta_n. \tag{10}
\]
Repeating (7)--(8) with the events \(\{u_0\in I_n^U(y_0)\}\) and \(\{u_n\in I_n^U(y_0)\}\) yields, under the boundary law, probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\) that
\[
 \operatorname{diam}I_n^U(y_0)
 \ge |u_n-u_0|
 =1-e+e\delta_n
 \ge1-e, \tag{11}
\]
which is the upper-endpoint assertion.  Strict positivity \(0<e<1\) from \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\) makes the fixed lower bound \(1-e\) positive and ensures both treatment conditionals used below are defined.

It remains to verify that the assumed close alternatives are genuinely available in the graphical model.  Write \(\Delta_z\) for the unit point mass at \(z\).  For the first boundary, choose \(z_+>y_0\) and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), define
\[
 \widetilde P_n=(1-\delta_n)P_0+\delta_n\Delta_{z_+}.
\]
Because \(P_0(({-}\infty,y_0])=1\), one has \(\widetilde P_n(({-}\infty,y_0])=1-\delta_n\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(\widetilde P_n,P_0)=\delta_n\).  Keep the propensity \(e\) and the off-arm observed law \(S=\mathcal L(Y\mid A\ne a)\) fixed.  The resulting one-observation laws are
\[
 \nu_0=e(\Delta_a\otimes P_0)+(1-e)(\Delta_{1-a}\otimes S),
 \qquad
 \nu_n=e(\Delta_a\otimes\widetilde P_n)+(1-e)(\Delta_{1-a}\otimes S),
\]
so \(\operatorname{TV}(\nu_n,\nu_0)=e\delta_n\).  The telescoping identity
\[
 \nu_n^{\otimes n}-\nu_0^{\otimes n}
 =\sum_{k=1}^n
 \nu_n^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes(\nu_n-\nu_0)
 \otimes\nu_0^{\otimes(n-k)}
\]
and the triangle inequality for the total-variation norm give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\nu_n^{\otimes n},\nu_0^{\otimes n})
 \le n\operatorname{TV}(\nu_n,\nu_0)
 =ne\delta_n=o(1). \tag{12}
\]
For each \(n\), realize \(\nu_n\) by drawing \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), drawing \(Y(a)\sim\widetilde P_n\) and \(Y(1-a)\sim S\) independently of \(A\), and setting \(Y=Y(A)\).  With latent variable \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), this is a nonparametric latent-variable SCM Markov to the bow ADMG and it satisfies consistency.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)=\widetilde P_n
 =\mathcal L(Y(a)),
\]
so the mutual-absolute-continuity condition holds.  Equivalently, \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) certifies the interventional law \(Q_n=\widetilde P_n\) because it has the admissible representation \(Q_n=e\widetilde P_n+(1-e)\widetilde P_n\).  Thus the alternatives are members of the bow-SCM class.  For the second boundary, choose \(z_-\le y_0\) and use \(\widetilde P_n=(1-\delta_n)P_0+\delta_n\Delta_{z_-}\); since \(P_0(({-}\infty,y_0])=0\), the same argument gives \(F_{\widetilde P_n}(y_0)=\delta_n\) and (12).

Because \(1-2\alpha>0\), (9) or (11) contradicts convergence of the relevant projection diameter to zero in boundary-law probability.  The conclusion applies to every rectangular band, hence also to any band produced through the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\): such a band cannot be both uniformly covering and shrinking on a class containing these support contacts.  The theorem therefore rules derivative-based shortening out on tie-inclusive local classes, while \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}sample\text{-}simultaneous\text{-}band}\) supplies the stated honest fallback.  Throughout this argument \(0<e<1\); the algebraic value of the endpoint maps at \(e=0\), used only when clipping the finite-sample propensity interval, is not invoked.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are independent random variables satisfying \(0\le Z_i\le1\) almost surely and \(\mu=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m E[Z_i]\), then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\left|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m Z_i-\mu\right|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: If X1,...,Xn are independent random variables with ai <= Xi <= bi for all i, then for any epsilon > 0, Pr(|Xbar-E[Xbar]| >= epsilon) <= 2 exp(-2 n^2 epsilon^2 / sum_i (bi-ai)^2).

upstream.citation: Wassily Hoeffding, Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables, JASA 58(301):13-30 (1963), DOI 10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830
upstream.locator: Theorem 2; two-sided form by applying the one-sided bound to Xi and -Xi and summing the two tails

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement checked in the publicly accessible UC Berkeley repository author copy of Ben-David et al., Machine Learning 79 (2010), Proposition 1, which explicitly identifies it as Hoeffding's inequality; setting ai=0, bi=1 yields the cited node (strict > follows from >=). Primary source is Hoeffding 1963 Theorem 2.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent real random variables with common distribution function \(F\), and \(\widehat F_m\) is their empirical distribution function, then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}|\widehat F_m(y)-F(y)|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

source.locator: Section 2.14, Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality with Massart's sharp constant
source.verbatim_statement: Let Fhat_n denote the empirical distribution function for n iid observations with distribution function F. Then Pr(sqrt(n) sup_x |Fhat_n(x)-F(x)| > lambda) <= 2 exp(-2 lambda^2), without restriction on lambda.

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\{Q:P\ll Q,\ dP/dQ\le1/e\ Q\text{-almost surely}\}\). Every representation \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary probability law \(R\) is realized by a latent bow-ADMG construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), without imposing mutual absolute continuity.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), a treatment arm \(a\), and a standard Borel outcome space \(\mathcal Y\).   First omit the mutual-absolute-continuity restriction and let \(Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\).  By consistency,
\[
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P.
\]
Define the probability law \(R=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\).  The law of total probability and \(\Pr(A=a)=e\) give
\[
 Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))=eP+(1-e)R. \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(Q\in\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Notice that no support condition on \(R\) was used.

Conversely, suppose \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for an arbitrary probability law \(R\) on \(\mathcal Y\).  Since \(\mathcal Y\) is standard Borel, one may construct a joint probability law as follows.  Draw \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\); conditionally on \(A=a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(P\); conditionally on \(A\ne a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(R\).  Draw \(Y(1-a)\), conditionally independently given \(A\), from any fixed probability law on \(\mathcal Y\).  Put
\[
 U=(A,Y(0),Y(1)),
\]
let the treatment structural equation return the first coordinate of \(U\), and let the outcome structural equation be \(Y=Y(A)\).  The common latent input \(U\) represents \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), and the explicit treatment input in the outcome equation represents \(A\to Y\).  Hence the construction is Markov to the bow ADMG in \(\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure}\).  It satisfies consistency, has propensity \(e\), has observed arm law \(P\), and (1) gives interventional law \(Q\).  Therefore \(Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\), proving
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P). \tag{2}
\]

We next prove the cap characterization.  If (1) holds, then \(Q(B)\ge eP(B)\) for every measurable \(B\).  Consequently \(P\ll Q\).  For \(r=dP/dQ\), the measure inequality \(eP\le Q\) implies \(er\le1\), \(Q\)-almost surely; otherwise integrating \(er-1\) on the positive-measure set where it is positive would contradict \(eP\le Q\).  Thus \(r\le1/e\).  Conversely, suppose \(P\ll Q\) and \(r=dP/dQ\le1/e\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  Define
\[
 R(B)=\frac{Q(B)-eP(B)}{1-e}.
\]
The numerator has nonnegative \(Q\)-density \(1-er\), so \(R\) is a nonnegative countably additive measure.  Moreover,
\[
 R(\mathcal Y)=\frac{1-e}{1-e}=1,
\]
and hence \(R\) is a probability law and \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  Together with (2), this proves
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)
 =\left\{Q:P\ll Q,\ \frac{dP}{dQ}\le\frac1e\quad Q\text{-almost surely}\right\}. \tag{3}
\]

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\), fix a threshold \(y\), and put \(p=F_P(y)\). In the unrestricted bow class, \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\}=[L^{\to}_e(p),U^{\to}_e(p)]=[ep,ep+1-e]\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\). In the mutual-AC bow class, \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\), with unique value zero at \(p=0\) and one at \(p=1\). Every endpoint is attained in its stated support regime, including at atoms; boundary endpoints outside the mutual interval require singular residual laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(y\in\mathbb R\), let \(B=(-\infty,y]\), and put \(p=P(B)=F_P(y)\).  In the unrestricted bow class, \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) gives \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary \(R\).  Thus, writing \(s=R(B)\),
\[
 F_Q(y)=Q(B)=ep+(1-e)s. \tag{20}
\]
Both \(B\) and \(B^c\) are nonempty.  A point mass at any point of \(B\) has \(s=1\), a point mass at any point of \(B^c\) has \(s=0\), and mixtures of these two laws attain every \(s\in[0,1]\).  Hence, for every \(p\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\}
 =[ep,ep+1-e]=[L^{\to}_e(p),U^{\to}_e(p)]. \tag{21}
\]
The unrestricted construction in the completeness theorem supplies an attaining bow SCM for each value.  When \(p=0\) or \(p=1\), an endpoint requiring mass on a \(P\)-null side is attained by a singular residual law and therefore does not satisfy mutual absolute continuity.

Now impose the mutual-AC condition.  The mutual corollary \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) gives exactly the representations (20) with \(R\ll P\).  If \(0<p<1\), define
\[
 R_1(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B)}p,
 \qquad
 R_0(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B^c)}{1-p}.
\]
Both laws are absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), and they satisfy \(R_1(B)=1\) and \(R_0(B)=0\).  Their convex mixtures attain all \(s\in[0,1]\), so the mutual interval is \([ep,ep+1-e]\).  If \(p=0\), absolute continuity forces \(R(B)=0\), and (20) is uniquely zero.  If \(p=1\), it forces \(R(B^c)=0\), and (20) is uniquely one.  At either boundary \(R=P\) is an admissible attaining residual law.  These are precisely the piecewise values in \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\):
\[
 \{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]. \tag{22}
\]
Every residual law used for (22) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), so the mutual construction in the completeness theorem gives an attaining SCM satisfying all four maintained assumptions.  The argument is eventwise and does not assume that \(P\) is atomless; in particular an atom at \(y\) causes no change.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), one-sided exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\) and write \(c=1/e\).  For \(P\ll Q\), let \(r=dP/dQ\).  Then \(\int r\,dQ=1\), so addition of \(b(t-1)\) to a generator changes neither \(D_f(P\|Q)\) nor \(B_f(e)\).  Convexity gives
\[
 f(t)\le\left(1-\frac tc\right)f(0)+\frac tc f(c),\qquad 0\le t\le c. \tag{15}
\]
For \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary probability law \(R\), the domination \(Q\ge eP\) implies \(P\ll Q\) and \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  Integrating (15) gives \(D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P) \tag{16}
\]
for every admissible generator.

If \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\), choose the affine representative \(g\) which is zero on \([0,c]\) and strictly positive above \(c\).  Then \(B_g(e)=0\).  If \(Q\in\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\), nonnegativity of \(g\) and affine invariance imply
\[
 0\le\int g(r)\,dQ=D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)=0.
\]
Thus \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  The measure \((Q-eP)/(1-e)\) is a probability law because it has nonnegative \(Q\)-density \((1-er)/(1-e)\).  Hence \(Q\in\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Together with (16), this proves universal exactness.

For necessity, universal exactness implies exactness for every full-support binary \(P\).  On a full-support binary alphabet the support distinction disappears: arbitrary residual binary laws are automatically absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\).  We nevertheless give the boundary argument explicitly.  For \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), \(p\in(0,1)\), the law \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(ep)\) is in \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Every \(Q_q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\) with \(0<q<ep\) violates \(p/q\le c\), so it is outside \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Exactness and continuity in \(q\) therefore force
\[
 D_f(P\|Q_0)=B_f(e). \tag{17}
\]
At the boundary the ratios are \(c\) and \(t_p=(1-p)/(1-ep)\).  Letting \(p\downarrow0\) in (17) gives \(B_f(e)=0\).

Set \(g(t)=f(t)+f(0)(t-1)\).  The radius identity gives \(g(0)=g(c)=0\), and \(g(1)=0\).  Equation (17) then gives \(g(t_p)=0\) for every \(p\in(0,1)\), hence \(g=0\) on \([0,1]\).  Given \(y\in(1,c)\) and \(x\in(0,1)\), set \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\).  Construct full-support binary \(P,Q\) with likelihood ratios \(y,x\) and \(Q\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\).  The ratios have mean one and are at most \(c\), so \(Q\in\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Exactness, convexity at the mean, and \(B_g(e)=0\) yield
\[
 0=g(1)\le \lambda g(y)+(1-\lambda)g(x)=D_g(P\|Q)\le0,
\]
whence \(g(y)=0\).  Thus \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\).  Convexity implies \(g(t)\ge0\) for \(t>c\).  If equality held at some \(t>c\), the same two-ratio construction would give \(D_g=0\) but would violate the cap, contradicting exactness.  Hence \(g(t)>0\) above \(c\), so \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).

This proves the three-way equivalence.  The one-sided bow-mixture completeness theorem identifies \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) with \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\), giving the stated graphical interpretation.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of full-support binary pairs \((p,q)\) such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) and simultaneously \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\). If \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\), the set can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\); otherwise a normalized representative vanishes on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), and the set can be chosen inside the zero-divergence face. This includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(c=1/e\) and let
\[
 \ell(t)=\left(1-\frac tc\right)f(0)+\frac tc f(c),
 \qquad \ell(1)=B_f(e).
\]
If \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\), convexity implies the strict chord inequality \(f(x)<\ell(x)\) at every \(x\in(0,c)\): otherwise the nonnegative concave function \(\ell-f\), zero at both endpoints, would have an interior zero and concavity would force it to vanish everywhere.  Choose \(x\in(0,1)\), set
\[
 \lambda=\frac{1-x}{c-x},\qquad q_0=\lambda,\qquad p_0=c\lambda,
\]
and take \(P_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\), \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_0)\).  Their likelihood ratios are \(c,x\), with respective \(Q_0\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\), and hence
\[
 D_f(P_0\|Q_0)<\lambda\ell(c)+(1-\lambda)\ell(x)=\ell(1)=B_f(e). \tag{18}
\]
Choose \(q_1<q_0=ep_0\) sufficiently close that the strict inequality in (18) persists.  By continuity, there is a nonempty open neighborhood \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of \((p_0,q_1)\) on which simultaneously \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\) and \(p/q>c\).  Every pair has full support, so the mutual and one-sided divergence-ball support requirements both hold, while the violated likelihood-ratio cap excludes the pair from both mixture classes.

If instead \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), normalize it by an affine term to obtain a convex \(g\) that vanishes on \([0,c]\).  Convexity gives \(g\ge0\) above \(c\).  Since \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), there exists \(d>c\) with \(g(d)=0\), and convexity then gives \(g=0\) throughout \([0,d]\).  Choose \(x\in(0,1)\), \(y\in(c,d)\), and \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\).  The full-support binary pair with likelihood ratios \(y,x\) and \(Q\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\) satisfies \(D_f=D_g=0=B_f(e)\) and violates the cap.  A sufficiently small open neighborhood keeps both likelihood ratios in \((0,d)\) and the first above \(c\); throughout it the divergence remains zero and both mixture classes remain violated.  On full-support binary alphabets every residual law is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), so the mutual and one-sided mixture classes coincide there.  This proves the simultaneous dichotomy, including its nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear cases.  It also supplies the stable witness promised by the failure direction of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}generator\text{-}iff\text{-}frontier}\).

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\). On a finite alphabet that retains cells outside \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), adding \(q_j\ge ep_j\) to the divergence program gives exactly this unrestricted lawful class, weakly tightens every linear bounded-query optimization, and strictly tightens it whenever the relaxed optimizer is unique and violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), the success-indicator query has a strict one-sided legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational binary laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), set \(c=1/e\), and let \(f\) be admissible.  If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for an arbitrary probability law \(R\), then \(Q\ge eP\).  Hence \(P\ll Q\), \(r=dP/dQ\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  Convexity on \([0,c]\) gives
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le\int\left\{\left(1-\frac rc\right)f(0)+\frac rc f(c)\right\}dQ
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e).
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\), and the definition of the one-sided lawful correction gives
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\cap\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P).
\]
The one-sided bow-mixture completeness theorem identifies the last class with \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\).

On a finite alphabet, including cells with \(p_j=0\), a probability vector \(q=(q_j)_j\) belongs to \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) exactly when
\[
 q_j\ge ep_j\qquad\text{for every }j. \tag{19}
\]
One direction follows from \(q_j=ep_j+(1-e)r_j\).  Conversely, (19) makes \(r_j=(q_j-ep_j)/(1-e)\) a nonnegative probability vector and yields \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  It also ensures \(P\ll Q\).  The preceding divergence inequality shows that the divergence constraint is redundant after (19) is imposed.  Hence the capped program has exactly the unrestricted lawful class.  The capped set is compact; restricting to it weakly tightens every linear maximum or minimum.  If an attained relaxed optimizer is unique and violates (19), equality of optimal values would make a capped optimizer a distinct relaxed optimizer, which is impossible.  Thus the tightening is strict in the stated case.

For \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), the construction in \(\mathrm{thm:support\text{-}regime\text{-}open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\) supplies a nonempty open set of full-support binary pairs with \(q<ep\) that are feasible for the one-sided divergence ball.  After shrinking to a rectangle, its projection contains a nonempty open interval of observational probabilities \(p\), and for each such \(p\) some feasible \(q<ep\) remains.  For the success indicator, the lawful lower value over (19) is \(ep\), while the relaxed lower value is at most \(q<ep\).  This proves the strict one-sided legality gap.

statements.statement: Let \(e_1,e_2\in(0,1)\) with \(e_1\ne e_2\). No single finite continuous convex generator \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\) is universally exact at both propensities: it is impossible to have \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e_i}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{e_i}(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) and both \(i=1,2\). Equivalently, \(\mathfrak H_{1/e_1}\cap\mathfrak H_{1/e_2}=\varnothing\). In contrast, the adaptive family \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\) belongs to \(\mathfrak H_{1/e}\) and is exact stratum by stratum, in both the one-sided and mutual-absolute-continuity regimes.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(c_i=1/e_i\) for \(i=1,2\).  If a single generator \(f\) were universally exact at both propensities, \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}generator\text{-}iff\text{-}frontier}\) would give
\[
 f\in\mathfrak H_{c_1}\cap\mathfrak H_{c_2}. \tag{20}
\]
Assume without loss of generality that \(c_1<c_2\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak H_{c_i}\) supplies \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
 f(t)=b_i(t-1),\qquad 0\le t\le c_i.
\]
Because \([0,c_1]\) contains points other than \(1\), these two identities force \(b_1=b_2=:b\).  The representative \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) therefore vanishes on \([0,c_2]\).  But membership in \(\mathfrak H_{c_1}\) requires \(g(t)>0\) for every \(t>c_1\), contradicting its vanishing on \((c_1,c_2]\).  Thus (20) is impossible.

For the positive result, fix \(e\in(0,1)\) and let \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\).  This function is finite, continuous, and convex, satisfies \(f_e(1)=0\), vanishes on \([0,1/e]\), and is strictly positive above \(1/e\).  Taking \(b=0\) in the definition gives \(f_e\in\mathfrak H_{1/e}\).  The one-sided frontier theorem therefore gives exactness at that stratum, and the mutual-absolute-continuity frontier theorem gives exactness in the mutual regime as well.

statements.statement: For every admissible \(f\), the Assumption-4 and positive-density classes are the reverse-support intersections of the literal one-sided classes: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\), and \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\). On every full-support binary alphabet the corresponding one-sided and mutual classes coincide.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a nonparametric bow-ADMG SCM in a fixed covariate stratum.
sampling_model.units: \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed; potential outcomes and the latent confounder are unobserved.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity \(0<e<1\) and mutual absolute continuity \(P\sim Q\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(e\) by the arm fraction and \(F_P\) by the empirical CDF within arm \(a\); the finite-sample band uses Hoeffding and conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz radii.

estimand_functional: Without reverse absolute continuity, \(Q_a\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\{eP+(1-e)R:R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\}\) with \(F_{Q_a}(y)\in[L^{\to}_e(F_P(y)),U^{\to}_e(F_P(y))]\); under Assumption 4, \(Q_a\in\mathfrak M_e(P)=\{eP+(1-e)R:R\ll P\}\) with \(F_{Q_a}(y)\in[L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y))]\)

tldr: The flagship result classifies exactly when the mutual-absolute-continuity version of the Jung--Kang \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class equals the compatible binary-treatment bow-SCM fiber for every law: modulo affine generator terms, \(f\) must vanish through the propensity cap and be strictly positive above it. Bow-mixture completeness, \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\), supplies the structural input, and a universal open illegal binary region supplies the stable converse, with explicit KL and hinge certificates. Exact atom-aware CDF endpoints, bounded-query support functions, simultaneous bands, and the \(\texttt{itbound}\) and IHDP legality correction are consequences and implementation layers.

project_justification.gap: Jung and Kang prove that every compatible interventional law belongs to a propensity-calibrated ambiguity class and optimize exactly over that class, yielding valid outer causal bounds; they do not establish that every ambiguity-class member is realizable by a bow SCM. Robust-statistics and information-theory papers separately provide contamination neighborhoods, hinge divergences, density bands, and finite-alphabet reductions, but none identifies all ordinary convex generators whose calibrated class exactly equals the bow-SCM law class or proves an open illegal region for every failure.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a generator-level causal legality frontier: a necessary-and-sufficient affine-invariant condition, with stable counterexamples when it fails and explicit causal endpoints when the exact cap is imposed.
project_justification.fill: The propensity-hinge iff is the sole flagship. Bow-SCM mixture completeness supplies its structural input, and the nondifferentiability-robust binary open-gap theorem supplies its stable converse, including explicit KL and hinge certificates. Sharp CDF and bounded-query formulas, distribution-free confidence bands, and the shared software cap are consequences and implementation layers.

related_work: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that every compatible interventional law lies in the propensity-calibrated \(f\)-divergence ambiguity class, and their later optimization is exact relative to that class. Those ambiguity-class extrema are valid outer causal bounds; the paper does not establish that every member is realizable by a bow SCM, whereas the flagship target characterizes exactly when the ambiguity class equals the compatible bow-SCM fiber. This proposal uses the mutual-absolute-continuity version under their Assumption 4: their equation (10) visibly states only \(P\ll Q\), while the maintained model and density parametrization supply \(Q\ll P\). Sason and Verdu (2016) supply affine normalization, bounded-relative-information, and \(E_\gamma\)-hinge machinery that motivates the cap-detecting direction. Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014, Theorem 2.1 and Section 3) show why divergence geometry can be exposed on small alphabets, while the proposed necessity proof specializes the boundary analysis to a binary propensity cap. Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018, main theorem and Discussion) equate least-favorable robust tests under divergence balls and constructed density bands and explicitly leave set equality and generator recovery open; the proposed iff resolves that question for the one-sided propensity band. Chen, Berrett, Damoulas, and Caprio (2026, Proposition 2.3) identify Huber contamination with a linear-vacuous credal ball, which establishes the noncausal mixture geometry but not the ordinary \(f\)-generator frontier or bow-SCM realization. Duarte et al. (2024) certify sharp causal bounds by response-function polynomial programs for discrete variables; the proposed latent construction is analytic and covers general standard Borel outcomes. Dorn and Guo (2023) provide the closest econometric precedent for repairing an over-wide sensitivity optimization by imposing the exact compatible weighting class. Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) and Fang and Santos (2019) motivate the uniform and derivative-aware inference layer, respectively.
technical_internal_limitation: Pointwise attainment of \(L_e(F_P(y))\) and \(U_e(F_P(y))\) permits the attaining residual law to depend on \(y\). It does not imply that the entire lower or upper envelope is itself one counterfactual CDF. The complete process identified set remains \(\{eF_P+(1-e)F_R:R\ll P\}\), so any reported whole curve must retain a common residual CDF.
honest_scope: The mixture characterization and endpoint algebra have short candidate arguments, but every result remains \(\mathrm{to\text{-}prove}\) at this stage. The load-bearing open content is the fully quantified necessity and open-illegal-region dichotomy for finite continuous convex generators with kinks or extended zero faces. The finite-sample band is deliberately conservative at support contacts; asymptotically exact tie-adaptive inference is isolated as \(\mathrm{oeq:tie\text{-}adaptive\text{-}exact\text{-}band}\). The mixture and SCM classes and the endpoint maps alone extend to the boundary \(e=1\), where \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\) and \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\). No all-generator singleton claim is made for calibrated divergence classes at \(e=1\): a zero-radius \(f\)-class is a singleton only under an additional strict Jensen-equality or cap-detecting condition, and affine or identically zero generators are counterexamples. The flagship iff remains explicitly fixed at \(0<e<1\). The empirical IHDP deliverable is a reproducible before-and-after audit, not a theorem about the benchmark.
